mechanism_coverage: test_sync_preparing_delete_tail_settles_without_content_activity exercises mechanism 1 by accepting sync-preparing only after Task 2 has established no content need, and mechanism 5 by proving fresh LocalIndexUpdated and sequence churn no longer re-arms settlement.

test_content_only_settlement_rejects_unsafe_folder_states and test_sync_preparing_content_only_settlement_keeps_runtime_errors_blocking prove that syncing, scanning, error, paused, pull-error, and watch-error states still block despite the narrow PREPARING_STATES exception.
design_decisions: settled now separates content presence from diagnostic status. It accepts only idle or PREPARING_STATES and keeps status and update_in_progress unchanged, so delete-only sync-preparing tails can settle while still reporting PREPARING.

LocalIndexUpdated and sequence-change quiet windows were removed only from settlement because their events contain no action. Fresh local changes, scan progress, and a recent content ItemFinished remain quiet-window blockers.
active_transfer remains a settled blocker to preserve the post-game peer-completion and outbound-observation safety contract even when there is no remote progress object.

settled is shared by pre-game and post-game. Therefore post-game can now settle during sync-preparing and cleaning when peer content is complete, whereas it previously required idle. This is safe and matches the v0.4.4 decision that local snapshot-pruning deletes must not gate completion: content is present, no download or remote-progress activity remains, and syncing still blocks.
task_4.results: Task 4 is complete. A delete-only sync-preparing tail can settle as soon as content is complete, while content need, active content, unsafe states, runtime errors, and post-game confirmation holds remain blocking.

design_decisions: Pre-game diagnostics compare exactly the reported phase, folder state, need bytes, content-item count, pending deletes, active download-file count, active-item count, and settled value. They emit at INFO only when that tuple changes.
The diagnostic reads the computed ActivityStatus and FolderRuntime but does not add device IDs, folder identifiers or paths, item names, or raw API data to the line.

The replay drives SyncthingWatch._tick and SyncthingWatchManager.poll_watch rather than calling _tick_sample directly. Each of its three roughly two-second batches contains delete start and finish events followed by a sequence-advancing LocalIndexUpdated event.
unverified: Real device behaviour remains unverified; this round used unit and replay coverage only, not a Steam Deck or live Syncthing folder.
Syncthing versions other than v2.1.2 remain unverified; a future version could route deletions through syncing instead of sync-preparing.
The needBytes-reaches-zero-before-commit in-flight temporary-file hazard has no live reproduction, although content-item counts continue to gate it.
Whether the 3.0-second pre-game settle window is the correct operational value remains unmeasured on a device.
The pre-game stall window and the frontend and backend ceilings remain untouched and unproven on hardware.
